questions.prompt: A client exceeds its rate limit. What should the API return?

options.text: 429 Too Many Requests, with a Retry-After header

questions.explanation: 429 tells the client it's being limited, and Retry-After tells it when to try again. A 500 wrongly suggests the server is broken.

questions.prompt: A token bucket has capacity 10 and refills 2 tokens per second. It's full. A client sends 15 requests at once. How many are allowed immediately?
questions.explanation: A full bucket allows a burst up to its capacity: 10 requests. The other 5 are rejected; the bucket then earns 2 tokens each second.

questions.prompt: A fixed window limiter allows 100 requests per minute. What's the most a client can send within a 2-second span?

options.text: 200, by sending 100 just before a minute boundary and 100 just after

questions.explanation: Each calendar minute has its own counter, so the end of one window and the start of the next can both be used fully. Sliding windows avoid this.

questions.prompt: A payment request times out and the client retries. Which make the retry safe? Select all that apply.

options.text: The client sends the same idempotency key on the retry
The server stores each key with its result and returns the stored result for a repeat
The client generates a new idempotency key for the retry
A unique constraint on the key stops two simultaneous requests from both charging

questions.explanation: The key must stay the same across retries so the server can recognize the repeat. A new key makes the retry look like a new payment.

questions.prompt: Ten thousand clients lose their connection at the same moment and retry with exponential backoff but no jitter. What goes wrong?

options.text: Nothing; exponential backoff alone spreads the load
They all retry at the same instants, so the recovering server gets synchronized waves of traffic

questions.explanation: Clients that failed together compute the same backoff, so they retry together at 100 ms, 200 ms, 400 ms and so on. Random jitter spreads them out.
